title: Philadelphia Fed Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations (ATSIX), December 2026 — 2:00 p.m. ET on the Tuesday after Christmas, the one 2026 ATSIX date a rule actually derives, and a live long-end month only in a sample that ended in 2008
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 130,695 bytes) and parsed as data this session — the embedded release payload holds 237 rows across 18 families, of which exactly 12 are ATSIX, every one at 2:00 p.m., the December row verbatim {"title":"Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations","month":"december 2026","day":"29","displayMonth":"Dec","year":"2026","time":"2:00 p.m."}. THE DATE IS DERIVED THIS SESSION, which no other 2026 ATSIX row manages: ten of twelve rows are their month's last Friday; December's last Friday is 2026-12-25, Christmas Day, a federal holiday on which the Reserve Banks are shut (christmas-market-closure-2026-12-25 on this shelf); the next business day is Monday 2026-12-28 and the bank effectively does not publish on Mondays — 3 of its 237 2026 rows fall on a Monday (1.3%), none of them in December, and 2026-12-28 carries zero Philadelphia Fed releases of any family. Last Friday, skip the holiday, skip Monday, gives Tuesday 2026-12-29 exactly. The same weekday arithmetic was reproduced here rather than recalled. Filed estimate on three counts, none of which is doubt about the date: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own data schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms, and no ATSIX-specific page carries a forward date — the landing page (fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200, 36,808 bytes) stamps itself '28 Aug '26', matching the calendar's Aug 28 row and the published workbook's last vintage (2026-08), and defers forward dates to the shared calendar
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-10 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal for this id (proposals/aruoba-inflation-term-structure-2026-12-29.from-livingston-survey-2026-12-11.json, filed 2026-09-09) and discharged both tasks it assigned, plus the claim it was filed on. TASK (a) — DISCHARGED, and the premise CORRECTED: the proposal said the 2026 calendar 'shows only 11-20 and 12-29, which is not obviously monthly'. The same endpoint on the same day carried all TWELVE 2026 ATSIX rows, Jan 30 through Dec 29, every one at 2:00 p.m. The cadence is unambiguously monthly; the proposer under-read its own payload. The date derivation is in `source` and is this event's one advantage over its November sibling, whose row no rule explains. TASK (b) — ALREADY SETTLED by a sibling on 2026-09-09: ATSIX is model output, not a survey (aruoba-inflation-term-structure-2026-11-20.json), and its family was declined there on measurement. THE PROPOSAL'S OWN CLAIM IS REFUTED: it filed this row as 'the first curve read AFTER the FOMC, the CPI and the cliff all resolve'. The technical note's item 7, fetched and text-extracted this session, confines market data to the OTHER sheet — 'For computing the real interest rate yield curve, we use the nominal yield curve averaged over the first 15 calendar days of the month' — so the published inflation-expectations curve contains no market data at all; it is a factor fit over survey forecasts whose earliest input, SPF Q4, closed on 2026-11-16, three weeks before fomc-2026-12-09. AND THE REASON THE SIBLING LEFT THIS ROW STANDING DOES NOT SURVIVE ITS OWN ERA SPLIT: the Mar/Jun/Oct/Dec long-end seasonal decays monotonically — ratio 2.68 (t=5.93) in 1998-2008, 1.65 (t=2.16) in 2009-2016, 1.39 (t=1.75) in 2017-2025 — and December alone in 2017-2025 moves the 10-year point 0.0493pp against 0.0443pp for every other month, ratio 1.11, t=0.27. In the era the spreadsheet is genuinely real-time, December is an ordinary month. Impact LOW and symbols [] on the same grounds the sibling measured and this session re-measured: no house playbook is macro-keyed, no tracked name carries an expected-inflation channel, and the 14:00 ET slot sits inside the year-end illiquid week with 28 tracked events within five days, a 7-year note auction the same afternoon (treasury-7y-note-2026-12-29) and FOMC minutes the next (fomc-minutes-2026-12-30). This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and this ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
